analysis.rationale: R1 signal reinterpretation: a blur_glass:2 simulation on the same clean image reproduces every target signal to near-identical values (variance_ratio 0.8338 vs 0.8346, contrast_spread 0.8745 vs 0.8745, residual_intensity_corr -0.5284 vs -0.5243, gm_ratio 0.5038 vs 0.5039, glass_score 0.470 vs 0.468, sigma 1.85 vs 1.85, block_boundary 1.0021 vs 1.0026). The 'gamma suspect' and low-confidence YCrCb noise signals are therefore glass-shuffle/blur-residual signatures, not missing degradations: brightness gamma/shift sev1 would move the mean by >=25/255 (observed -0.6/255), and contrast_weaken_scale:1 would scale variance by 0.5625 (observed 0.835, no discrete global severity fits with mean unchanged). Severity: R1 5-pair scan shows glass:1 mean 32.71 dB (CI 10/6/7/7/8) and glass:3 mean 31.58 dB (CI 9/7/7/8/7), both below R0's glass:2 5-pair mean 34.21 dB (CI 10/10 on 5/5); R1 pair0 re-check of glass:2 reproduced 30.27 dB with CI 10/10 and all metric diffs 0.000. No candidate approaches >40 dB or +2 dB over the previous round, so decision is NO_CHANGE. The low trained support PSNR (27.66 dB) is expected for glass:2 rather than evidence of misidentification: x_distortion glass performs random local pixel transpositions (shuffle_pixels_njit), which destroy local pixel order irreversibly, capping restoration PSNR.
